issues.legal_issue: A constitutional challenge to a statutory provision must be presented in the context of sufficient case-specific facts rather than in the abstract.
material_facts: The petitioner challenged the validity of a rent-control provision but did not identify the premises he owned or explain the grievance in relation to those premises.
The High Court dismissed the petition in limine.
issues.conclusion: The petition was rightly rejected because the essential facts needed to examine the constitutional challenge were lacking, and the Court would not interfere with that rejection.
issues.legal_principle: A challenge to the constitutional validity of a provision must arise in the context of relevant facts and cannot be decided in the abstract or a vacuum. The Court relied on this principle without citing an earlier case.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A person brought a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of a legal provision.
predicates.lacks_case_specific_property_facts: The challenger did not provide particulars of the property or other case-specific facts needed to assess the claimed injury.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity challenge lacks case-specific facts needed to assess it, the challenge is rejected for that lack.

issues.legal_issue: Differences between the rent-regulation laws of different States do not, by themselves, make one State's law invalid under Article 14.
material_facts: The petitioner argued that rent-fixation provisions in other States were fairer, more just, and more reasonable than the challenged provision.
The challenged law and the laws from other States had been enacted by different legislatures, each choosing a method it considered suited to its State.
issues.conclusion: Article 14 does not permit a State law to be struck down merely because its provisions differ from those of laws on the same subject in other States.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not authorize invalidating one State's law through a comparative study of laws enacted by different legislatures, and legislative choice among methods suited to different States is not a ground for challenging validity. The Court relied on Prabhakaran Nair v. State of Tamil Nadu and others, [1987] 4 SCC 238.

predicates.state_law_validity_challenge: A person brought a proceeding challenging the validity of a law enacted by a State legislature.
predicates.cross_state_comparison_only: The challenger relied on differences between the challenged law and laws on the same subject enacted by other States.

issues.definition: When a State-law validity challenge rests only on differences from other States' laws, those differences alone do not invalidate the challenged law.

issues.legal_issue: A rent-control scheme that uses earlier local rents as a basis for fixing fair rent is not unreasonable per se merely because prices later rose or other States used different methods.
material_facts: The challenged rent-control law was enacted in 1949 and used rents prevalent for similar accommodation in the locality during 1938 as the basis for determining basic rent.
The scheme permitted specified increases over basic rent.
The law's stated object included restricting increases in rent.
The petitioner relied on later price rises and on different rent-fixation methods used in other States.
issues.conclusion: The scheme was not unreasonable per se, and the challenge to the rent-fixation provision on the grounds advanced was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that legislative choices about fair-rent methods are not invalidated by comparison with methods chosen elsewhere; whether a particular method is suited to local conditions is for the relevant legislature. In light of the law's stated rent-restriction objective, its use of earlier local rents with specified increases was not unreasonable per se. The Court referred to Article 14 and Article 19(1)(g), distinguished M/s Raval & Co. v. K.C. Ramachandran and others, AIR 1974 SC 818, [1974] 2 SCR 629 as arising in a different context, and also referred to Prabhakaran Nair v. State of Tamil Nadu and others, [1987] 4 SCC 238.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_rent_control and earlier_local_rents_used_as_baseline and permitted_rent_increases and rent_restriction_object

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_rent_control: A person brought a proceeding challenging the constitutionality of a rent-control scheme.
predicates.earlier_local_rents_used_as_baseline: The scheme based rent fixation on rents previously prevailing for similar accommodation in the locality.
predicates.permitted_rent_increases: The scheme allowed specified increases over the baseline rent.
predicates.rent_restriction_object: The scheme was enacted with the stated object of restricting rent increases.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a rent-control scheme that uses earlier local rents as a baseline, permits specified increases, and has a rent-restriction object, the scheme is not unreasonable per se.
